review_notes: I read the whole file and the IsL3Levi.mem_center_iff API in Ch6Sec1Lem4FusL3Lev.lean. I looked for repeated nontrivial reasoning. The only repetition I judged worth a finding is the "element of K centralising K, so it lies in Z(K), so it is 1 or z" argument, which appears in hy1 and hker. Other similarities are not worth extracting: hkN/hkN' in hDy are one-line applications, and isPGroup_subgroupOf/isPGroup_map are different arguments. I did not check the exact signature of IsL3Levi.exists_action; the shape of hσker is inferred from how it is used (hσker y hyn h1 and hσker _ _ hk). The proposed lemma and rewrites have not been compiled.

have hcen : k ∈ Subgroup.center ↥(leviOfL3 N z) := by
      rw [Subgroup.mem_center_iff]
      intro g
      apply Subtype.ext
      exact Subgroup.mem_centralizer_iff.mp hc (g : G) g.2
findings.problem: The same argument is written out twice in one proof. An element x of K := leviOfL3 N z that centralizes K (as a subset of G) is repackaged as an element of Subgroup.center ↥K by the Subtype.ext / mem_centralizer_iff / mem_center_iff boilerplate. Then IsL3Levi.mem_center_iff is applied to conclude x = 1 ∨ x = z. The first copy is in hy1 (lines 160–165, for ⟨y, hyK⟩). The second is in hker (lines 196–202, for k). Each copy then consumes the dichotomy in its own way. The two copies differ only in the element and in how the two cases are used, so the lifting step is duplicated inside a long proof.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma next to IsL3Levi.mem_center_iff, or as a private helper in this file:

theorem IsL3Levi.eq_one_or_eq_of_mem_centralizer {G : Type*} [Group G] {K : Subgroup G} {u : G} {p : ℕ} (hK : IsL3Levi K u p) {x : G} (hxK : x ∈ K) (hc : x ∈ Subgroup.centralizer (K : Set G)) : x = 1 ∨ x = u

Proof sketch: show `(⟨x, hxK⟩ : ↥K) ∈ Subgroup.center ↥K` by `rw [Subgroup.mem_center_iff]; intro g; exact Subtype.ext (Subgroup.mem_centralizer_iff.mp hc (g : G) g.2)`, then return `(hK.mem_center_iff ⟨x, hxK⟩).mp this`.

Use 1 (hy1). Replace lines 160–171 by `rcases hK.eq_one_or_eq_of_mem_centralizer hyK hc with h3 | h3`. Keep the two existing branches, `rw [h3, orderOf_one] at hy5; norm_num at hy5` and `rw [h3, hz2] at hy5; norm_num at hy5`.

Use 2 (hker). Replace lines 196–206 by `rw [Subgroup.mem_subgroupOf]; rcases hK.eq_one_or_eq_of_mem_centralizer k.2 hc with h2 | h2` followed by `· rw [h2]; exact S.one_mem` and `· rw [h2]; exact hzS`. The `hc` already has type `(k : G) ∈ Subgroup.centralizer (leviOfL3 N z : Set G)` at line 195, and `hyK` and `k.2` supply the membership argument. Both uses have the hypotheses the lemma needs.
findings.benefit: The centralizer-to-center-to-{1,z} reasoning gets one named statement, and the long proof loses about 14 lines of repeated boilerplate. The lemma also fits the existing IsL3Levi API and could be reused by other L3 fusion files that need the same step. The main proof then reads as a case analysis on x = 1 or x = z, not as Subtype plumbing.
